pageCache.pageTitle: Before and After School Care | Newport CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Newport CE Primary School
Before and After School Care
The school operates a breakfast club in the hall daily from 7:45 to the start of lessons.
Please contact the school office for further details or book through Tucasi Scopay.
Fun to Learn offer Breakfast, After-school and Holiday Club as well as Early Years care for children from 6 months
Early years care is offered 50 weeks a year except Bank Holidays and the Christmas period. We are open from 7.45 a.m. to 5.45 p.m.
Breakfast club opens at 7.45 am and children can have breakfast if they wish and play until it is time for school to start. Children are escorted to school by setting staff when their year group starts. Fees for Breakfast Club are charged at a single rate per morning.
After-school club - The children are collected from school at their individual finish times. Children can have a snack and drink if they wish and the club is open until 6 pm. Fees are again charged at a single rate per evening.
Holiday Club is open 7.45 a.m. to 5.45 p.m. during the school holidays throughout the year except for Bank Holidays and the Christmas period. Places can be booked by the hour to keep costs to parents as low as possible, but do need to be for a minimum period of 3 hours. Sessions need to be booked and paid for in advance.
For further details on any aspect of the childcare available please contact:
Michele Jones: Tel: 822371 between 7.45 am and 5.45 pm
Email: Michele@fun2learn.org.uk

STATUTORY RELATIONSHIPS & HEALTH EDUCATION
We include the statutory Relationships and Health Education within our whole-school PSHE/RHE Programme.
“Parents have the right to request that their child be withdrawn from some or all of sex education delivered as part of statutory Relationships and Sex Education” DfE Guidance p.17
At Newport CE School, puberty is taught as a statutory requirement of Health Education and covered by our SCARF Programme as part of the 'Growing and Changing' unit. We conclude that sex education refers to human reporduction, and therefore inform parents of their right to request their child be withdrawn from the PSHE lessons that explicity teach this:
Year 6 - making babies lesson
CLICK HERE for further information about the 'Growing & Changing' unit.

Information for parents
If you’re worried about anything to do with COVID-19, including support with self-isolation, local help is available.
Go to www.keeptheislandsafe.org or call the Isle of Wight’s COVID-19 helpline 01983 823600

Newport CE Primary School
Friends of Newport
All parents of the school are automatically members of the Parent Teacher Association in the school, known at Newport CE as the Friends of Newport (FON) and are invited to any FON events and meetings.
As we start each new year, the FON invite nominations for the roles of Chair, Secretary and Treasurer. These are important but rewarding responsibilities and further details of what each role involves are in an information pack which is available from reception. Each candidate needs to be nominated and seconded by a parent or teacher at the school.
The FON always welcome volunteers and helpers, so please come along even if you are only able to help out occasionally.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Houses | Newport CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Newport CE Primary School
School Houses
The children and staff are allocated into one of four house groups, These grouping arrangements may be used for events such as sports day or worships and as an organisational structure for other activities within the class. Each House has a variety of captain positions and the pupils selected work together with their House to encourage the community spirit, friendly competition and offer peer support.
House points (DoJo points) will be given to promote and encourage good learning and behaviour for a variety of reasons which include:
Our School’s four houses are named after four beautiful mythical creatures chosen by the children.
Griffin Phoenix Dragon Unicorn
Griffin reliable, trustworthy, protector, clever
Unicorn proud, intelligent, empathetic, peaceful
Phoenix honest, loyal, creative, smart
Dragon brave, wise, strong morals,
Children exemplifying positive behaviours
To reward and celebrate good work
Children who are ready to help
To those who collaborate well with others

pageCache.text:
Newport CE Primary School
School Uniform
All children should wear our school uniform to enhance the sense of belonging and equality.
We value a smart and tidy appearance.
You may select from:
Green sweatshirt, jumper or cardigan.
Grey pinafore, skirt or trousers
Gold polo shirt, blouse, or roll necked jumper.
Green and white checked dress
White, green or grey tights.
Shoes should be practical and sensible
– no trainers, boots or high heeled shoes.
Green sweatshirt or jumper.
Grey trousers / shorts
Gold polo shirt, shirt or roll necked jumper.
Grey, black or white socks
Shoes should be practical and sensible
– no trainers, boots or high heeled shoes.
A PE bag (drawstring bags are ideal) containing:
Bottle green shadow striped shorts
Bottle green tee shirt with logo
Black plimsolls or trainers for outdoor PE
Outdoor kit in the winter can include a tracksuit or jumper and leggings. Football boots and shin pads are necessary for football club and school matches.
All items of uniform should be named please.
Items are available for purchase from Kids & Co, 22 High Street, Ryde, Isle of Wight, PO33 2HW.
Telephone Number 01983 615244.
Website: www.kidsandcodirect.co.uk
The wearing of jewellery in school is not permitted at all for health and safety reasons, but if your child already has earrings, one small stud in each ear may be worn
